title: Cofferdam Overtopping Risk — Flood Frequency

P_exceedance.description: Probability of the design flood being exceeded during construction

T.description: Return period of diversion design flood

applicability: Example: 25-yr flood with 3-yr construction → P = 1-(1-1/25)³ = 11.5% chance of overtopping. USBR/USACE typically use 10–50 yr return period depending on consequences of overtopping.

title: Diversion Tunnel/Conduit — Discharge Capacity

Cd.description: Discharge coefficient (0.60–0.90 depending on intake shape and flow regime)

H.description: Head on diversion (headwater elevation - tailwater or centerline)

applicability: For submerged flow (inlet control or full-flow). For free-surface flow in tunnel, use Manning's equation with appropriate slope. Transition from free-surface to pressurized flow must be carefully analyzed.

title: Cofferdam Height Design

h_design_flood.description: Headwater elevation at diversion design flood (from routing)

h_settlement.description: Anticipated cofferdam settlement (0.3–1.0 m for earth coffers)

applicability: Headwater elevation determined by routing the diversion flood through the tunnel/conduit system with cofferdam in place. Higher headwater allows more flow through smaller diversion — trade-off between cofferdam height and tunnel size.

title: Diversion Tunnel Manning's Equation (Free Surface)

n.description: Manning's roughness (0.012–0.016 for concrete-lined, 0.025–0.040 for unlined rock)

applicability: For free-surface flow regime in diversion tunnel. Check that flow depth < 75% of tunnel diameter (otherwise transition to pressurized flow). Air demand becomes critical as depth approaches crown.

title: Stage-Discharge for Diversion System (Head-Discharge Curve)

Q_total.description: Total flow past dam site at headwater H

Q_tunnel.description: Flow through diversion tunnel/conduit at headwater H

Q_overtopping.description: Flow over cofferdam if headwater exceeds crest (weir equation)

applicability: Combined stage-discharge used for routing the diversion design flood. Tunnel transitions from free-surface to pressurized as headwater rises. Cofferdam overtopping adds capacity but may cause damage.

title: Cofferdam Seepage — Darcy's Law (Sheet Pile or Earth)

k.description: Hydraulic conductivity of foundation or cofferdam material

L_seepage_path.description: Length of seepage path (sheet pile depth, cofferdam base width)

applicability: For earth cofferdams, use flow net analysis. For sheet pile cofferdams, seepage occurs under the sheet piles — longer pile reduces seepage. Dewatering pumps must handle seepage + direct precipitation.

title: River Closure — Required Rock Size (Riprap Stability)

D_50.description: Median rock size for river closure

V.description: Velocity through the gap during closure

C_stability.description: Stability coefficient (0.7–1.2 depending on placement method)

applicability: During end-dumping closure, velocity through the narrowing gap increases. Rock size must increase as gap narrows. Critical phase is the final closure when velocity peaks. Pre-staged closure with multiple dumping points reduces peak velocity.

title: Dewatering Pump Capacity

Q_rainfall.description: Direct rainfall runoff into work area

applicability: Redundant pumping capacity required. Typically N+1 pump arrangement. Sump sizing for intermittent pumping. Emergency power backup essential.
